notes: Coverage: 55 BetterTouchTool mappings, one live hidutil remap and 59 terminal mappings, source-checked 2026-11-04. Terminal editing is installed and conditional on a new or reloaded zsh session; existing shells need reload. Configuration verification is not a successful live-key test.

BTT coverage retains all 44 shortcuts and 11 typed sequences: 37 enabled, 17 conditional and one disabled. All retained rows belong to active presets and none are Trash-linked. Enabled means the saved binding is on, not that its action passed a live test.

Consecutive keycaps are sequence steps; plus signs indicate a chord. Alphabetic sequence labels name physical keys, not required uppercase characters. Keyboard region selection and mouse selection are distinct; check each mapping’s conditions.

Key labels use the US/macOS virtual-key convention. Hardware filters and non-US layouts remain unverified. Seven named targets exist only in inactive presets; explicit dispatch, overlapping seek thresholds and brightness conflicts remain untested. See each row’s limitations.
Private expansion text, clipboard contents, saved destinations, network identities and executable payloads are withheld. Insert saved text (private) deliberately does not reveal its content.
No custom global menu accelerators or custom Claude/Codex keybindings were found in the inspected configuration. Per-app menu preferences and built-in shortcuts were not inventoried.

Action descriptions follow the stored action chains and named targets, not BTT’s container labels. Missing resume targets and unclear Spotify/Chrome behavior are retained and flagged, not repaired or omitted.

Existing terminal coverage includes 18 global iTerm mappings, eight profile mappings shared by both configured profiles, 20 zsh mappings and the live Copy Mode menu shortcut. Cmd+Shift+C remains Copy Mode; normal Cmd+C is unchanged. Cmd+Ctrl+C was verified unused before installation. Authenticated apply and a zero-change post-check verified the two owned iTerm bindings across 14 profile/session maps; no keystrokes were sent.

Emacs is the intentional zsh default; vi is optional. Terminal widgets passed fresh-login shell and isolated PTY checks without using the real clipboard. Existing shells must reload their configuration or be replaced by a new shell; installed configuration does not prove live shortcut behavior.

The Ctrl+A cut dispatcher inspects only already-pending input, with no added lookahead delay. It reads complete Unicode characters without a partial-character timeout and leaves KEYTIMEOUT unchanged. Same-write or already-pending Ctrl+A then Ctrl+K typeahead is indistinguishable from Cmd+X; delayed Ctrl+K keeps its native action.

Ctrl+Y is not promised to restore a terminal cut. Inspected Claude Code 2.1.314 maps it to chat:defaultToNewerModel; harness and tmux kill/yank behavior remains unverified. No harness bindings were changed.
Whole-line paste is enforced at paste time through a clipboard tag plus a BTT variable, matching VS Code and Sublime behavior.

entries.limitations: An untagged clipboard or unsupported field gets one normal Edit > Paste. If the caret, text or focus changed, or a paste is refused after an attempted press, nothing is pasted and a notification appears. The BTT variable, not the clipboard tag, may be stale after an ordinary copy; the tag wait applies only within about 1.5 seconds of a line copy or cut. Cut preserves the app's rich text when the copy matches. A missing Edit menu loses that Cmd-V: nothing is pasted, a notification appears, and interception stays off until the next line copy or cut. A Firefox copied blank line pastes inline. Firefox accepts either break form; contenteditable role and caret restoration remain unconfirmed live. Finder single-paste remains unconfirmed live. After reinstall, a fresh line copy or cut is required.

entries.action: Cut the logical line including its break, confirm removal, and tag the clipboard for whole-line paste.
entries.conditions: Editable caret with no selection; excludes configured code editors and terminal apps (including JetBrains). Otherwise the original shortcut passes through.
entries.limitations: Saved keyboard ID 0; its device identity/filtering semantics were not resolved. Requires Accessibility-readable/settable text; unsupported editors may refuse the operation. Firefox blank-line cuts are refused. After a confirmed cut, waits up to one second for the app clipboard; if its string matches the line plus one newline, RTF/HTML is retained, otherwise plain text plus one newline is written. A completed cut that cannot be tagged warns and pastes inline.

entries.conditions: A new or reloaded zsh session has loaded terminal-editing.zsh; its line editor owns input in emacs or vi insert mode. iTerm sends the installed Cmd+X mapping; removal requires a successful clipboard write.
entries.limitations: Outside zsh this sends Ctrl+A then Ctrl+K; in Vim normal mode Ctrl+A increments a number, so this is not universally safe cut. Ctrl+Y is not promised to restore it. In zsh the dispatcher consumes only already-pending input, with no added lookahead delay; it reads complete Unicode characters and leaves KEYTIMEOUT unchanged. Same-write or already-pending Ctrl+A then Ctrl+K typeahead is indistinguishable from Cmd+X; delayed Ctrl+K keeps its native action. An empty cut range preserves the clipboard. Native Ctrl+Space regions survive Ctrl+A; Shift-selection ends.
